sense: ordering in a café or restaurant

terms.grammar: the polite present subjunctive of volō, with the dish in the accusative
terms.comment: Velim, “I should like”, is the polite way of saying what one wants, everywhere in Cicero’s letters; see “want”. To a child: Quid vīs?
Sūmere of taking a meal (cibum sūmere, Lewis & Short s.v. sūmō).
Traupman’s waiter dialogue; we have found no classical instance of accipere for ordering a dish.

phrases.latin: Piscem assum velim, quaesō; puer pānem et cāseum vult.
phrases.english: I’d like the grilled fish, please; the boy wants bread and cheese.

phrases.latin: Quīn bene māne est. Itaque jentāculum sūmam, quaesō.
phrases.english: Why, it’s early in the morning. So I’ll have breakfast, please.

sources: Lewis & Short: volo · Lewis & Short: sumo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 67, 68.
